questions.stem: A 31 year old man has a 2 day history of gradually increasing pain at the back of his left testis and mild dysuria. He has a new sexual partner. His temperature is 37.6°C. The left epididymis is swollen and tender posteriorly, and it can be felt distinctly from the testis, which itself is non-tender and lies normally.
questions.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Gradual posterior pain with a tender epididymis that is distinct from a non-tender testis is isolated epididymitis.

steps.x: The question asks: Which is the most likely diagnosis? Decide what kind of answer you need before reading the options.

clues: gradually increasing pain at the back of his left testis
steps.x: Gradual onset, posterior tenderness, and the testis itself is spared.

elim: Painless and fluctuant, not tender with fever and dysuria.
Arises above the testis and you cannot get above it; the epididymis would not be tender.
Sudden severe pain with a high-riding, tender testis; this testis is non-tender and lies normally.
A painless 'bag of worms' above the testis, without fever or dysuria.

steps.x: B. Epididymitis. Tender epididymis palpable separately from the testis = isolated epididymitis.

questions.stem: A 29 year old man was diagnosed with left epididymitis 4 days ago but did not collect his antibiotics. The whole left side of his scrotum is now swollen, red and tender. His temperature is 38.2°C, pulse rate 98 bpm. The epididymis can no longer be felt separately from the testis. The cremasteric reflex is present.
questions.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Untreated epididymitis spreads into the testis: the swelling now involves both, so the epididymis is no longer distinct from the testis.

steps.x: The question asks: Which is the most likely diagnosis? Decide what kind of answer you need before reading the options.

steps.x: Known epididymitis that has progressed to involve the testis.

Painless, soft and transilluminates.
Sudden onset with an absent cremasteric reflex; this followed known epididymitis.
Painless and slowly growing, not febrile and acutely tender.

steps.x: B. Epididymo-orchitis. Epididymitis can progress to epididymo-orchitis, and then the two are not distinct.

questions.stem: A 58 year old man has a 3 day history of a painful, swollen right testis and fever. A week ago he had a urinary catheter removed after a knee replacement. He is married and monogamous. His temperature is 38.0°C, pulse rate 96 bpm. Urine dipstick shows leucocytes and nitrites.
questions.q: Which is the most likely causative organism?
questions.e: Over 35, epididymo-orchitis is usually caused by urinary pathogens: E. coli most often, then Klebsiella; recent catheterisation is a risk factor.

steps.x: The question asks: Which is the most likely causative organism? Decide what kind of answer you need before reading the options.
Older age, a recent catheter and a positive nitrite: a urinary organism.

elim: Typical under 35 and with STI risk; he is older, monogamous and recently catheterised.
Causes orchitis after parotitis in unvaccinated young men.
An STI organism, unlikely in an older monogamous man after catheterisation.
Not a usual cause of epididymo-orchitis.

steps.x: B. Escherichia coli. Over 35 or after catheterisation = E. coli.

questions.stem: A 22 year old builder attends a sexual health clinic with 2 days of a painful, swollen left testis and a thick yellow urethral discharge. He had unprotected sex with a new partner 5 days ago. His temperature is 37.9°C. A Gram stain of the discharge shows Gram-negative intracellular diplococci.
questions.q: Which is the most likely causative organism?
questions.e: Under 35, epididymo-orchitis is usually an STI: Chlamydia or gonorrhoea. Gram-negative intracellular diplococci and purulent discharge mean gonorrhoea.

steps.x: The question asks: Which is the most likely causative organism? Decide what kind of answer you need before reading the options.
A young man after unprotected sex with diplococci on Gram stain.

steps.x: E. Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Under 35 = STI; diplococci = gonorrhoea.

questions.stem: A 23 year old man has a 1 day history of a painful, swollen right testis. Six days ago he developed fever and painful swelling below both ears. He missed his childhood immunisations. He has not been sexually active for a year. His temperature is 38.3°C. Urine dipstick is negative.
questions.q: Which is the most likely causative organism?
questions.e: Orchitis is typically viral, classically mumps in unvaccinated young men, appearing 4 to 8 days after parotid swelling.

steps.x: The question asks: Which is the most likely causative organism? Decide what kind of answer you need before reading the options.
Parotitis a few days earlier in an unvaccinated man.

elim: He is not sexually active and has a negative dipstick.
Causes glandular fever with lymphadenopathy, not classic parotitis then orchitis.
A urinary pathogen of older men; the dipstick is negative.
He is not sexually active.

steps.x: D. Mumps virus. Parotitis then orchitis 4 to 8 days later = mumps.

questions.stem: A 36 year old man has a 3 day history of aching in his right scrotum that came on gradually. He has mild dysuria. His temperature is 37.5°C, pulse rate 84 bpm and BP 128/76 mmHg. The testis lies normally and the cremasteric reflex is present.

Tender epididymis palpable separately from the testis

Gradual onset, urinary symptoms, normal lie and reflex.

Describes a varicocele.

steps.x: E. Tender epididymis palpable separately from the testis. Epididymitis: posterior tenderness, epididymis felt separately.

questions.stem: A 46 year old man has a painful, swollen left testis for 2 days. He had a flexible cystoscopy and urethral catheter for a urinary retention episode 10 days ago. questions.e: Risk factors are unprotected intercourse, UTI and recent catheterisation, which introduce organisms that ascend to the epididymis.

steps.x: E. Recent urethral catheterisation. Catheterisation, UTI and unprotected sex are the risk factors.

questions.stem: A 52 year old man has been taking ofloxacin for 6 days for E. coli epididymo-orchitis. His pain has worsened and he still has fevers. His temperature is 38.6°C and pulse rate 106 bpm. The left hemiscrotum is red, hot and fluctuant. Ultrasound shows a hypoechoic collection within the testis.
questions.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Testicular abscess is a complication of epididymo-orchitis, suggested by failure to improve on antibiotics, fluctuance and an intratesticular collection.

steps.x: The question asks: Which is the most likely diagnosis? Decide what kind of answer you need before reading the options.

clues: worsened and he still has fevers

Would not develop days into a treated infection with a collection.
Painless and afebrile.

steps.x: C. Testicular abscess. Not improving on antibiotics + fluctuance = abscess.

questions.stem: A 39 year old man was treated for epididymo-orchitis 5 months ago. His fever and swelling resolved, but he still has a dull ache in the right scrotum most days. He has no urinary symptoms. His temperature is 36.8°C. The epididymis is mildly tender but not swollen. Scrotal ultrasound shows no mass, collection or varicocele.
questions.q: Which is the most likely cause of his symptoms?
questions.e: Chronic pain is a recognised complication of epididymo-orchitis, alongside abscess and infertility.

steps.x: The question asks: Which is the most likely cause of his symptoms? Decide what kind of answer you need before reading the options.
Persisting ache after treated infection with a normal scan.

elim: Would be visible or palpable and reducible.
Causes sudden, short episodes of severe pain.
Ultrasound shows no mass.
Ultrasound excludes it.

steps.x: A. Chronic pain after epididymo-orchitis. Complications: infertility, abscess, chronic pain.

questions.stem: A 44 year old man has a 2 day history of a painful, swollen, red right hemiscrotum and dysuria. The pain came on gradually. His temperature is 38.1°C, pulse rate 94 bpm and BP 132/80 mmHg. The right testis and epididymis are swollen and tender. Urine dipstick shows leucocytes and nitrites.
questions.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Unilateral painful, red, swollen scrotum with fever, dysuria and a positive urine test is epididymo-orchitis.

steps.x: The question asks: Which is the most likely diagnosis? Decide what kind of answer you need before reading the options.
Gradual pain, fever and an infected urine.

elim: Painless and transilluminates.
You cannot get above it and it is not associated with dysuria and fever.
Sudden severe pain without urinary infection.
Painless and slowly growing.

steps.x: A. Epididymo-orchitis. Painful swollen scrotum + fever + dysuria + positive dip = epididymo-orchitis.

questions.stem: A 19 year old man has a 2 day history of left scrotal pain that started gradually, with dysuria. He has had unprotected sex. His temperature is 37.8°C, pulse rate 88 bpm. When the left testis is gently lifted, his pain is clearly reduced. The cremasteric reflex is present and the testis has a normal lie.
questions.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: A positive Prehn's sign (pain relieved on elevation, by reducing venous congestion) favours epididymo-orchitis; in torsion the twisted pedicle means elevation does not help.

steps.x: The question asks: Which is the most likely diagnosis? Decide what kind of answer you need before reading the options.
Gradual onset, urinary symptoms and a positive Prehn's sign.

elim: Pain would not ease on lifting the testis, and you cannot get above a hernia.

Painless.

steps.x: A. Epididymo-orchitis. Prehn's sign positive = epididymo-orchitis, not torsion.

questions.stem: A 20 year old unvaccinated student developed bilateral parotid swelling and fever 2 days ago. Several students in his halls have the same illness. His temperature is 38.2°C. His testes are currently normal on examination. His university health centre confirms mumps. He asks when he might develop testicular pain if the infection spreads.
questions.q: Which is the most likely timing of orchitis after the onset of parotid swelling?
o: At the same time as the parotitis
questions.e: Mumps orchitis classically appears 4 to 8 days after parotid swelling, after haematogenous spread of the virus to the testis.

steps.x: The question asks: Which is the most likely timing of orchitis after the onset of parotid swelling? Decide what kind of answer you need before reading the options.
Mumps parotitis in an unvaccinated young man.

questions.stem: A 40 year old man comes to the emergency department with a 2 day history of a gradually painful, swollen left testis. He has mild dysuria. His temperature is 37.7°C, pulse rate 90 bpm and BP 130/78 mmHg. The epididymis is swollen and tender and the testis lies normally.

questions.e: The urine dipstick is the initial test in suspected epididymo-orchitis, followed by MSU culture or NAAT depending on age and risk.

For a painless testicular mass.

questions.stem: A 62 year old man has a painful, swollen right testis for 2 days. He has a long history of nocturia and a weak stream. He has been married for 35 years and has no other partners. His temperature is 38.0°C. Urine dipstick shows nitrites and leucocytes.

o: First-void urine NAAT for gonorrhoea and chlamydia
Mid-stream urine microscopy, culture and sensitivity

An older monogamous man with a likely urinary source.

questions.stem: A 24 year old man has a painful, swollen left testis and a urethral discharge. He has had several new partners. He passed urine just before arriving and cannot provide another sample for several hours. His temperature is 37.8°C.

questions.e: STI-related epididymo-orchitis is investigated with a NAAT for gonorrhoea and chlamydia on a urethral swab or first-void urine.

Does not identify the organism.

questions.stem: A 27 year old man has epididymo-orchitis. He had unprotected sex with a new partner 2 weeks ago. The nurse is about to give him a pot for a urine sample to test for gonorrhoea and chlamydia. He last passed urine 2 hours ago.

questions.stem: A 25 year old man has a 2 day history of a painful, swollen left testis and dysuria. He had unprotected sex with a new partner 2 weeks ago. questions.stem: After unprotected sex at a festival, a 21 year old man develops a painful, swollen right testis and urethral discharge over 3 days. His temperature is 37.8°C and pulse rate 90 bpm. questions.stem: A 30 year old man had chlamydial urethritis with dysuria and a clear discharge 2 weeks ago that he did not get treated. He now has a painful, swollen right epididymis that is tender posteriorly. His temperature is 37.6°C and pulse rate 86 bpm. The testis is not yet involved.
